correctness.rationale: The exact Fourier/hub-block decomposition gives all supported phases. For n congruent 2 mod 4 the opposite-parity canceling modes force \(\gamma^2=-1\), incompatible with the lambda pair and -2 mode. For n congruent 4 mod 8 the zero mode forces gamma=-1, incompatible with the same eigenphases. If n has an odd prime factor and is divisible by 8, zero sums of modes in two parity classes force simultaneously \(\gamma^p=1\) and \((-\gamma)^p=1\). For \(n=2^r\) with r>=4, the real cyclotomic basis is linearly independent of \(\sqrt{n+1}\); Kronecker gives a positive integer sequence aligning every Fourier and exceptional phase. At \(n=8\), the split frequency is integral and sqrt(2) supplies the sole irrational phase. Zero and -2 modes force a discrete time in the PST case, contradicting irrationality. Checks replay finite eigensystems and phase witnesses but the proof establishes the unrestricted statement.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior cycle theorem gives correct phases for the nonzero rim Fourier modes but has no condition to align the new hub eigenvalues. The present result proves independence of \(\sqrt{n+1}\) from a real two-power cyclotomic basis for \(n\ge16\) and handles \(n=8\) separately; those are not implied just by the cycle theorem. The negative wheel cases use common eigenphase identities and the new hub-block phase sum. Thus the general techniques are inherited, while the displayed closed classification is not an explicit prior corollary.

originality.rationale: Pal and Bhattacharjya prove the analogous cycle and complement theorem, but not the nonregular single-hub join, whose two exceptional eigenvalues must be approximated simultaneously. Coutinho et al. give a general PGST decision framework but no family-wide wheel classification. Kirkland and Monterde give the join spectrum and a complete PST theory, not the PGST classification. Full texts and named cross-slot database queries found no implication-equivalent published or indexed theorem. An unindexed earlier or later equivalent result is a residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent PGST-wheel theorem might be in a terminology variant, thesis, or publication not surfaced by these searches.
A general algebraic method can in principle decide any fixed graph, so the originality assessment is limited to the all-rim-order closed theorem rather than the existence of a decision algorithm.
The cyclotomic subfield lemma is standard algebra; no independent external mathematical review was performed.

value.rationale: The single-hub wheel is a natural, nonregular deformation of the cycle. The classification supplies a sharp all-orders iff theorem, distinguishes \(n=8\) from higher 2-powers via the new exceptional spectral frequency, establishes all negative cases, and shows that even when PGST survives, PST is destroyed. This is not merely an isolated low-order calculation or substitution in the cycle theorem; it resolves how a hub changes long-time transport across a full infinite family. It makes no claims about transfer-time bounds or other graph architectures.
